text: {"observations":"Speech occurs in bursts separated by pauses (~3.0-3.9 s, ~5.8-6.2 s, ~7.8-8.0 s). Bursts at 0.3-2.9 s, 4.0-5.7 s and 8.1-9.2 s all have a low fundamental of about 110-165 Hz with similar contours, consistent with one adult male voice. The burst at 6.3-7.6 s is clearly different: fundamental about 380-470 Hz with almost no energy below 300 Hz and strong 250-1000 Hz bands, consistent with a much higher-pitched second voice (child or woman). I found only these two distinct pitch registers, alternating in turns, which supports two speakers (C) and argues against one (A); there is no evidence of a third voice or of many voices (D, B).","answer":"C"}
